lesson.title: When multiplication makes a number smaller
lesson.content_md:
## The idea to rethink

Multiplication does not always make a number bigger. Multiplying by a fraction between 0 and 1 means taking only part of the original amount.

## A counterexample

Imagine **3/4 of a pizza**. Taking **1/2 of that amount** gives 3/8 of a pizza. Since 3/8 is less than 3/4, multiplying by 1/2 made the quantity smaller. On a number line, 3/8 sits to the left of 3/4.

## Try it

1. Without calculating first, decide whether 5/6 × 1/3 is greater or less than 5/6. Then calculate it.
2. Choose a number that you can multiply by 4/5 to get a result smaller than the starting number. Explain why your example works.
